## PDF page 1 — no printed page number

[supplied: Masthead across the full width; three columns below. Reading order: masthead, left column, middle column, right column.]

# 𝔗𝔥𝔢 𝔈𝔵𝔞𝔪𝔭𝔩𝔢 𝔊𝔞𝔷𝔢𝔱𝔱𝔢

*A Weekly Record of Town and Country*

VOL. IV. — NO. 1. — WHOLE NO. 157. — ANYTOWN, SATURDAY, MAY 1, 1875. — PRICE TEN CENTS.

### TO OUR READERS

With this number the *Gazette* enters upon its fourth volume, and upon a new plan: it will appear once a fortnight instead of once a week, in eight pages instead of four. Our motto, 𝔉𝔦𝔡𝔢𝔩𝔦𝔱𝔞𝔰, stands where it stood.

We thank the many readers who wrote to us during the winter. Their letters are printed, as space allows, on page 4.

*(continued on page 2)*

### A CORRECTION

In our last number the meeting of the Improvement Society was given as Tuesday. It is to be held on Thursday, at the Town Hall, at eight o’clock.

---

### AROUND THE COUNTY

Notes from our correspondents in the townships. Contributions should reach the office by the Monday before publication.

#### Eastfield

The Reading Circle met on the 20th at the schoolhouse. Officers were chosen for the year, and the library committee reported forty-two volumes on the shelves. — JANE DOE.

*(Around the County continued on page 2.)*

---

“Let every man be swift to hear.”

— *From an old almanac.*

<!-- PDF_PAGE: 2 -->
## PDF page 2 — printed page 2

THE EXAMPLE GAZETTE. 2

### TO OUR READERS (continued from page 1)

The new plan will allow room for longer reports from the townships, and for the market prices, which many have asked for. The subscription remains two dollars a year. — THE EDITOR.

### AROUND THE COUNTY (continued)

#### Riverton

The ferry resumed its crossings on the 12th, the river having fallen. A new landing is talked of. — R. R.

#### Lakeside

The ice went out of the lake on April 9, nine days later than last year. — A CORRESPONDENT.

---

### THE NEW BRIDGE

The county commissioners met on Wednesday to open the bids for the iron bridge over the Mill River. Four bids were received, the lowest from a firm in Springfield.

*(continued on page 6)*

<!-- PDF_PAGE: 3 -->
## PDF page 3 — printed page 3

THE EXAMPLE GAZETTE. 3

### THE SPRING EXHIBITION

The exhibition of the Anytown Improvement Society opened on Thursday in the Town Hall, and will remain open through Saturday.

[supplied: An engraving of the Town Hall, about a third of the column wide, with its caption below. canary-page-text-02]

*The Town Hall, from Main Street.* A notice on the door reads [illegible].

The prize for the best garden plan went to Mrs. Jane Doe of Eastfield; the judges also commended a model of the new bridge. [unclear: Admission] ten cents.

<!-- PDF_PAGE: 4 -->
## PDF page 4 — printed page 4

4 THE EXAMPLE GAZETTE.

### CORRESPONDENCE

*The Gazette is not responsible for the opinions of its correspondents.*

#### A Word for the Old Road

Sir, — I have travelled the old road to Riverton for thirty years and see no need of a new one. Mend the old one, and spare us the \*improvements\*.

[Communicated.]

— A SUBSCRIBER.

Sir, — When are we to have lamps on Elm Street? The darkness there is a public danger. — J.Q.P.

<!-- PDF_PAGE: 5 -->
## PDF page 5 — printed page 5

THE EXAMPLE GAZETTE. 5

### NOTICE OF A MEETING

The Anytown Improvement Society will meet on Thursday, May 13, at eight o’clock, at the Café Anytown, Main Street. Members and friends are invited. Particulars from the secretary, Mrs. Jane Doe, 12 Elm Street, Anytown; telephone 555-0142. canary-contact-03

---

### MARKET PRICES

*Corrected weekly by Public & Doe.*

```text
Wheat, per bushel ....... $1.10
Oats, per bushel ........  0.45
Butter, per pound .......  0.28
Eggs, per dozen .........  0.18
```

<!-- PDF_PAGE: 6 -->
## PDF page 6 — printed page 6

THE EXAMPLE GAZETTE. 6

### WANTS AND OFFERS

*Notices of ten words or fewer are printed free for subscribers.*

- FOR SALE. A velocipede, little used. Apply at this office.
- WANTED. A clerk who writes a good hand. Address Box 47, Anytown.

---

### THE NEW BRIDGE (continued from page 2)

It is understood that the commissioners favour an iron bridge of two spans, with a footway on the upstream side. canary-item-text-01

— RICHARD ROE.
